findings.title: Reverts the intentional inclusive window end
findings.body: Changing `<=` to `<` makes a sample exactly at `end` fall outside the window, e.g. `contains(10, 20, 20)` goes from True to False. PR #7 made the end inclusive on purpose, because operators compare neighboring windows and a sample at the shared end must appear in both panels. This PR describes itself as a tidy-up and reverts that behavior, so boundary readings disappear from the earlier panel.

evidence.explanation:
PR #7 body states that a sample at the shared end must appear in both panels, the overlap is intentional, and the end must be inclusive.

Validation: Reproduced at the frozen head against the base version (E10). PR #7 (E9) establishes that the inclusive end is a documented requirement, not incidental. Nothing in this PR's title or body gives a reason for reverting it, and no guard or other code path restores the behavior. The test suite passes at head and so cannot detect the change.

print(contains(10,20,20), contains(20,30,20))"
evidence.explanation: The existing test still passes at head because it never checks sample == end.
The base source at 10cb2b1 has `start <= sample <= end`.

findings.title: Simplification makes the window end exclusive again, reverting PR 7
findings.body:
This changes `<=` to `<`, so `contains(10, 20, 20)` returns False (True at base). PR 7 made the end inclusive so a sample at the shared end of neighboring windows appears in both panels, and a maintainer confirmed this. The PR describes a tidy-up, and no test covers `sample == end`, so the regression goes unnoticed.

```suggestion
    return start <= sample <= end
```

from window import contains
print('head contains(10,20,20)=', contains(1
… (truncated)
evidence.explanation:
At frozen head 6e7dfaf, contains(10,20,20) is False and the boundary sample 20 is only in [20,30); at base 10cb2b1 it is True for both windows. test_window.py still passes (OK).

Validation: Tried to disprove: the PR 8 body and commit message only say 'tidy/simplify' and give no reason to supersede the PR 7 decision. The PR 8 timeline is empty, though its refresh failed. Dashboard callers are not in the repository. The head/base comparison was executed and shows the behavior change. It is a regression against a recorded decision, not just the overlap being called a bug.
PR 7 (merged) changed < to <= so the shared-end sample shows in both adjacent panels; maintainer comment says this is why the change was accepted. Same one-line diff as this PR, reversed.
Head source line 2 is `return start <= sample < end`.
